research_rationale:
Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/(MIRROR_)DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming this order number, a date and subject agreeing with the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. EO 7278 (January 23, 1936), read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (two held copies of the same page, sha256 shared), exempts William H. Ramsey, senior attorney, Justice from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until February 1, 1937. Identity: number, date, person and title agree across the APP page, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. Later orders further exempting the same person are held and added to this packet as source-supplement excerpts: EO 7545 (January 29, 1937) recites EO 7278 and further exempts Ramsey until February 1, 1938. Each is recorded as a later event on the clause (clauses.csv). Extension reading, decided on the texts: each later order is a new exercise of the section 204 proviso with its own period. None says that the earlier order 'is amended' or alters its date; each recites the earlier exemption as a past grant ('who was exempted ... by Executive Order No. ...') and grants a further exemption 'until' a new date. EO 7645 confirms the reading by counting the earlier orders as separate 'periods totaling three years and eight months'. The strike-and-insert ruling does not apply because nothing is struck or inserted. So this order's own command ended on its own stated date, inclusive (exclusive alternative: ended when that day began), and each extension is recorded as a later event naming the same employee; the employee's exempt status continued without a gap under the extension orders. The alternative reading, that the extensions prolonged this order's command, would put its first end at the last extension's 'until' date (1938-02-01, inclusive); the texts do not support it, because no extension operates on this order's text. Legal reading: ends by its own terms on 1937-02-01, inclusive. The census, WPA and full-text name searches found no further order naming this person after the last extension. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 after this date (for example EO 7725 of October 1937, under section 204, running to November 1, 1938), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.
